page.layout: One printed page. Running head at top with page number 236 at left. Main text in full-width paragraphs (Latin, each followed by a German line in black letter), with woodcut illustrations of shells interspersed on the right and centre. No marginal notes. Catchword "CONCHA" at lower right.

main_text.p: CONCHA striata altera Rondeletij, similis priori: nisi quòd illa aliquot lineas tantùm à latere ad latus per striarum transuersum ductas habet. hæc non lineas simplices, sed virgas latas sicuti fascias per transuersum ductas habet. est etiam rufa: unde Concha striata, fasciata, & rufa dici potest.

p.bl: GERM. Ein andere Streym˯muscheln/mit übertwá ren breitlachten gleych als bendlen. ist von farb rotlacht.

main_text.p: CONCHA striata tertia Rondeletij. Hæc (inquit) cæteris longior est, oui figura: testis multùm cauis, canaliculis parum profundis, aliquot lineis per transuersum ductis.

p.bl: GERM. Das dritt geschlecht der Streym˯muscheln.

main_text.p: CONCHIS striatis Rondeletij subieci speciem illam, quã Venetijs rotundæ nomine pictam accepi. Rondeletius primam è tribus striatis suis rotundam uocat.

p.bl: GERM. Widerumb ein Streym˯muschel/ hat vilicht kein vnderscheid von der vorge setzten ersten oder andern.

main_text.p: IN stagnis quoq; marinis reperiuntur Conchæ nonnullæ, & Cochleæ: ea maximè rotunda & striata, quam hîc expressimus, Rondeletius. atqui positas ab eo figuras duas Concharum, non Cochlearum generis esse apparet, ut in uerbis eius sic legendum coniciam: In stagnis quoque marinis reperiuntur Cochleæ nonnullæ, & Conchæ, &c.

p.bl: GERM. Seemuscheln/wie die iñ gesalzŋen sehen bey dem meer gefunden werden.

main_text.p: CONCHA Crassæ testæ, & Conchulæ uariæ Rondeletij. A Galade & Chama aspera (inquit) hæc Concha crassitudine tantùm testarum differt. Hæ lineis aliquot à latere ductis distinctæ sunt, nihilominus tamen læues sunt.

p.bl: GERM. Ein art der Glattmuscheln/ den nåchstgenañten gleych/aber von schalen dicker.

page.notes: Woodcut illustrations of shells (five figures) are not transcribed as text. The German lines are set in black letter and are transcribed as such; some may contain doubtful letters. Printing irregularities in the German are left as printed.
